Good practice data is the fuel of every project. The twenty sources below are free, famous and reliable. Some give you a CSV with one click; others need an API call, a Python package or a SQL query. This guide shows **what each source is good for** and **exactly how to pull data from it**. 🚀

::: {.callout-tip}
## 🎯 What you will get
- 🗂️ A filterable catalogue of 20 open data sources
- 🧭 A decision flow for choosing the right extraction method
- 💻 Copy-ready extraction code for downloads, APIs, Python packages, SQL and cloud buckets
- 🔄 An animated extract → clean → store pipeline and a worked, simulated example
- ⚖️ Notes on licences, rate limits and good manners
:::

## 📝 Note
The FRED **CSV link** works without a key, for example `fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE` ([FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE)); the full **API** needs a free key ([FRED API docs](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/)).
:::

## 💻 Extraction recipes

Each tab is a working pattern. Replace dataset codes and keys with your own. Keys belong in environment variables, never in notebooks you share.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## 📥 Direct download

```python
import pandas as pd

# Our World in Data: every chart has a CSV
le = pd.read_csv(
    "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy.csv")

# FRED: one series, no key needed
unrate = pd.read_csv(
    "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE",
    parse_dates=["observation_date"])

# NYC TLC: copy a monthly Parquet link from the TLC page
trips = pd.read_parquet("<paste-yellow-tripdata-link>.parquet")
```

## 📦 Python packages

```python
# UCI repository
from ucimlrepo import fetch_ucirepo          # pip install ucimlrepo
wine = fetch_ucirepo(id=109)
X, y = wine.data.features, wine.data.targets

# OpenML through scikit-learn
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml
titanic = fetch_openml("titanic", version=1, as_frame=True).frame

# Hugging Face
from datasets import load_dataset            # pip install datasets
imdb = load_dataset("imdb", split="train").to_pandas()

# Kaggle (token in ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json)
# kaggle datasets download -d blastchar/telco-customer-churn --unzip
```

## 🌐 REST APIs

```python
import os, requests, pandas as pd

# World Bank: no key; JSON when format=json
url = ("https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/US;IN;BR"
       "/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD")
page = requests.get(url, params={"format": "json",
                                 "per_page": 500}).json()
meta, rows = page                        # [paging info, records]
gdp = pd.json_normalize(rows)[["country.value", "date", "value"]]

# FRED API: free key in an environment variable
obs = requests.get(
    "https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations",
    params={"series_id": "CPIAUCSL", "file_type": "json",
            "api_key": os.environ["FRED_API_KEY"]}).json()
cpi = pd.DataFrame(obs["observations"])

# SEC EDGAR: no key, but identify yourself
hdr = {"User-Agent": "Your Name your.email@example.com"}
apple = requests.get(
    "https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000320193.json",
    headers=hdr).json()
```

## 🗺️ Geospatial

```python
import requests, pandas as pd

# OpenStreetMap Overpass: cafés in central Austin
query = """
[out:json][timeout:25];
node["amenity"="cafe"](30.25,-97.76,30.29,-97.72);
out;
"""
r = requests.post("https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter",
                  data={"data": query}).json()
cafes = pd.DataFrame([{"name": e["tags"].get("name"),
                       "lat": e["lat"], "lon": e["lon"]}
                      for e in r["elements"]])
```

## 🗃️ SQL (BigQuery)

```python
# pip install google-cloud-bigquery ; gcloud auth application-default login
from google.cloud import bigquery
client = bigquery.Client(project="your-project-id")
sql = """
SELECT name, SUM(number) AS babies
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE year >= 2000
GROUP BY name ORDER BY babies DESC LIMIT 10
"""
top_names = client.query(sql).to_dataframe()
```

## ☁️ Cloud buckets

```bash
# AWS Open Data and Common Crawl allow anonymous access
aws s3 ls s3://commoncrawl/crawl-data/ --no-sign-request

# copy one file to your machine
aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/<path>/file.parquet . --no-sign-request
```
:::

BigQuery gives every project the **first 1 TB of queries per month free**, and Google pays to store the public datasets ([Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/public-data)). NOAA's API needs a token in the request header and allows **5 requests per second and 10,000 per day** ([NOAA](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/webservices/v2)).

## 🔄 The extraction pipeline, animated

Real projects wrap extraction in a small pipeline so it can be re-run safely. Press play and follow a batch of records.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof playPipe = Inputs.toggle({label: "▶ Play animation", value: true})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pipeState = ({t: 0})
pipeTick = {
  while (true) { yield pipeState.t; if (!playPipe) return; pipeState.t = (pipeState.t + 1) % 300; await Promises.delay(40); }
}
{
  const stages = [["🌐", "Extract", "API, file, SQL"], ["✅", "Validate", "schema, nulls, ranges"], ["🧹", "Clean", "types, units, duplicates"], ["💾", "Store", "Parquet, database"], ["📊", "Analyse", "charts, models"]];
  const W = 780, H = 190, xs = stages.map((_, i) => 70 + i * (W - 140) / 4);
  const dots = d3.range(6).map(k => { const p = ((pipeTick + k * 50) % 300) / 300 * 4; const s = Math.floor(p), f = p - s; return {x: xs[s] + (xs[Math.min(4, s + 1)] - xs[s]) * f, bad: k === 2 && p > 1 && p < 1.15}; });
  const active = Math.floor((pipeTick % 300) / 300 * 5);
  return htl.svg`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;max-width:${W}px;font-family:Inter,system-ui,sans-serif">
    <line x1="${xs[0]}" y1="70" x2="${xs[4]}" y2="70" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity="0.2" stroke-width="4"/>
    ${stages.map(([ic, nm, sub], i) => htl.svg`<g>
      <circle cx="${xs[i]}" cy="70" r="34" fill="${i === active ? ms.indigo : "currentColor"}" fill-opacity="${i === active ? 0.85 : 0.08}"/>
      <text x="${xs[i]}" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="26">${ic}</text>
      <text x="${xs[i]}" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">${nm}</text>
      <text x="${xs[i]}" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.7">${sub}</text></g>`)}
    ${dots.map(d => htl.svg`<circle cx="${d.x}" cy="${d.bad ? 22 : 30}" r="7" fill="${d.bad ? ms.rose : ms.teal}"/>`)}
    <text x="${W / 2}" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.7">Green: good records · Red: a record rejected at validation</text>
  </svg>`;
}
```

## 🧪 Worked example: cleaning API data (simulated)

APIs rarely return a tidy table. Below we **simulate** a World Bank-style JSON response for five fictional countries, with typical problems: nested fields, values as strings, missing years and one unit error. Then we clean it in a few lines.

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly.express as px
from ms_charts import COLORS, PLOTLY_CONFIG
rng = np.random.default_rng(4)

# --- simulate a nested API response (fictional countries) ---
countries = [("Aurelia", 120), ("Borealis", 80), ("Caldera", 45),
             ("Deltora", 30), ("Equinox", 15)]
records = []
for c, start in countries:
    level = start
    for year in range(2005, 2026):
        level *= 1 + rng.normal(0.035, 0.025)
        # values arrive as strings, about 6% are missing
        v = None if rng.random() < 0.06 else str(round(level * 1e9))
        records.append({"country": {"id": c[:2].upper(), "value": c},
                        "date": str(year), "value": v})
# one record has a unit error (1000x too big)
if records[30]["value"] is None:
    records[30]["value"] = "1e9"
records[30]["value"] = str(float(records[30]["value"]) * 1000)

# --- clean ---
df = pd.json_normalize(records)                  # flatten nested JSON
df = df.rename(columns={"country.value": "country"})
df["year"] = df["date"].astype(int)
df["gdp_bn"] = pd.to_numeric(df["value"]) / 1e9  # strings → numbers
med = df.groupby("country").gdp_bn.transform("median")
df.loc[df.gdp_bn > 20 * med, "gdp_bn"] = np.nan  # drop the unit error
df["gdp_bn"] = df.groupby("country").gdp_bn.transform(
    lambda s: s.interpolate(limit_direction="both"))  # fill gaps
print(f"{df.value.isna().sum()} missing values filled, 1 unit error fixed")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-gdp
#| fig-cap: "Cleaned, simulated GDP series for five fictional countries."
#| code-fold: true
fig = px.line(df, x="year", y="gdp_bn", color="country", markers=True,
              color_discrete_sequence=[COLORS["indigo"], COLORS["teal"], COLORS["amber"], COLORS["rose"], COLORS["violet"]])
fig.update_layout(height=380, yaxis_title="GDP (billions, simulated)", xaxis_title=None, legend_title=None)
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

## 🛡️ Be a good data citizen

| Rule | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| 📜 Read the licence | Some data cannot be used commercially or needs attribution | Check the source's terms page; cite it in your charts |
| ⏱️ Respect rate limits | Too many calls get you blocked | Sleep between calls, use bulk downloads when offered |
| 💾 Cache what you fetch | Re-downloading wastes time and quota | Save raw responses to Parquet or JSON with a date |
| 🔑 Hide your keys | Leaked keys get abused | Environment variables, `.env` files in `.gitignore` |
| 🧾 Record provenance | You must be able to reproduce results | Log URL, parameters and download date |
| 🔐 Protect people | Even open data can identify individuals | Aggregate, drop identifiers, follow privacy rules |

A small helper that caches and retries covers most needs:

```{.python filename="fetch.py"}
import time, json, pathlib, hashlib, requests

def fetch_json(url, params=None, cache="raw", retries=3):
    h = hashlib.sha1(f"{url}{params}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    key = pathlib.Path(cache) / f"{h}.json"
    if key.exists():
        return json.loads(key.read_text())          # cached copy
    for attempt in range(retries):
        r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=30)
        if r.status_code == 429:                    # rate limited
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt); continue
        r.raise_for_status()
        key.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        key.write_text(r.text)
        return r.json()
    raise RuntimeError("Gave up after retries")
```

## 🧩 Summary

- Start with **Kaggle, UCI, OpenML and Hugging Face** for ML practice; use **FRED, World Bank, Eurostat, Census and OWID** for economics and society; **NOAA, NASA and OSM** for climate and maps; **BigQuery, AWS and Common Crawl** for big data.
- Pick the extraction method from what the source offers: **download → package → API → SQL or bucket**.
- Flatten, convert, validate and **cache** what you fetch.
- Follow **licences, rate limits and privacy** rules.
- Put the data to work with a [learning path](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) 🛤️.
